title: Xcode 27.2 Introduces an Agent- and Merge-Friendly JSON Format for Project Configuration
gist: Xcode 27.2 introduces an open-source JSON project format (xcode-project-format) replacing the plist-based project.pbxproj with project.xcproj, aimed at fewer merge conflicts, cleaner diffs and easier inspection by AI coding agents.

insights.claim: Apple's Xcode 27.2 replaces the property-list-based project.pbxproj with a JSON-based project.xcproj format, aimed at better readability, easier maintenance and easier understanding and modification by AI coding agents.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Apple is reshaping core developer tooling to be agent-friendly, a sign of AI coding adoption in the iOS toolchain.
insights.locator: Apple is introducing a new JSON-based format

insights.claim: The open-source xcode-project-format makes committed project changes reviewable because diffs correspond to the developer's actions in Xcode, and its stable, predictable representation reduces merge-conflict likelihood.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Fewer conflicts lower friction for multi-developer iOS teams.
insights.locator: The open source JSON file format

insights.claim: The JSON schema covers targets, file tree, build configurations, build settings and external dependencies, supports cross-subtree relationships, and favors human-readable names and paths over opaque identifiers, except for targets and build products which keep identifiers for external references.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Readable names make the format easy for scripts and agents to parse and edit.
insights.locator: At the top-level, JSON schema defines

insights.claim: Apple released a Swift package, XcodeProjectFormat, for encoding and decoding the new format, e.g. loading an XCSchema.Project from JSON data to list its targets.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: A first-party library lowers the barrier for third-party tool support.
insights.locator: To help developers work with the new format

insights.claim: iOS developers welcomed the change as long overdue: Nikita Dyachkov called project-file merging a long-standing problem for multi-developer teams, Khushal Jhalani a huge quality-of-life improvement, and Moumita China said it could have saved years of merge conflicts.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Strong community demand suggests rapid adoption.

insights.claim: Migration only changes the on-disk representation, not the underlying model, but teams should first check that tools including fastlane, CocoaPods and Tuist support the new format.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Third-party tool support is the main migration risk and a dependency for adopters.
insights.locator: Existing projects can be migrated easily
